incidents.victim: Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network — "Click to Pray" app
incidents.vector: An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in an unauthenticated API endpoint let anyone enumerate user records by ID.
incidents.impact: 700,000+ user names, emails, and account details exposed in plaintext; the flaw remained live and unpatched as of publication despite a researcher's disclosure attempt.

incidents.victim: Zimbra Collaboration Suite users — U.S. and allied government/commercial organizations, with extensive targeting of Ukrainian entities
incidents.vector: Zero-day (CVE-2025-66376) stored XSS in Zimbra webmail triggered by simply viewing a malicious email, loading a credential- and session-token-harvesting tool.
incidents.impact: Attackers exfiltrated victim email directories and up to 90 days of mailbox contents from unpatched Zimbra instances; campaign active since at least July 2025 despite a November patch.

incidents.vector: An autonomous AI agent, run in an unrestricted mode, was used to conduct the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Breach discovered after a researcher found an internet-exposed attacker directory containing malware payloads and intrusion logs.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached a supplier and pivoted into a platform shared with Stadler.
incidents.impact: The Everest ransomware group is demanding roughly 10 million Swiss francs (~$12.3M); Stadler says it will not pay.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed — company is investigating a security breach.
incidents.impact: Possible exposure of customer data under investigation; disclosed via an ASX filing.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed — hackers stole customer information.
incidents.impact: Stolen data was used to fraudulently rent furniture and electronics on the Acima marketplace, totaling roughly $13 million in fraudulent loan agreements.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Exposed sensitive customer data, including the last four digits of payment cards.

incidents.vector: Exploited a smart contract handling transactions between the Cardano and Binance blockchains.
incidents.impact: Nearly $10 million in crypto assets stolen within an eight-minute window before the platform could react.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly obtained some of the bridge's private keys to sign fraudulent transactions.
incidents.impact: $24 million in cryptocurrency stolen.

incidents.vector: Exploited the same vulnerable smart contract function and bug class as a prior hack, with a different wallet/attacker.
incidents.impact: $7.5 million in Ether stolen; the platform's second hack this year after an $11.5 million loss in May 2026.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators (Water/Wastewater Systems, Energy, Government Services and Facilities sectors)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers (Rockwell Automation, Schneider Electric, and Siemens) via malicious project-file interactions and manipulation of HMI/SCADA displays.
incidents.impact: Operational disruption and financial loss reported across affected U.S. critical infrastructure operators; advisory updated with detection guidance for malicious code hidden in reusable PLC code modules.

incidents.vector: Mass chaining of two newly disclosed vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030) to achieve remote takeover, beginning just three days after public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Widespread exploit attempts against one of the largest attack surfaces on the internet, dubbed "WP2Shell"; full compromise scope still emerging.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed — hackers accessed Fairlife production-related systems.
incidents.impact: Production halted at Fairlife's U.S. factories (Canadian lines unaffected); disclosed via SEC filing, with no group having claimed responsibility yet.

incidents.vector: Compromise reportedly followed exposure to the "Shai-Hulud" npm supply-chain worm.
incidents.impact: Internal files, source code, and detailed scraping instructions dumped online, revealing large-scale scraping of copyrighted songs from streaming platforms.

incidents.victim: Contractor to India's Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KNPP)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed — contractor compromised by an extortion group.
incidents.impact: Sensitive files related to the nuclear facility leaked online.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) servers, part of a broader campaign against Oracle EBS customers.
incidents.impact: Customer data stolen; breach disclosed to state regulators nearly a year after it occurred. This is Estée Lauder's second breach after a 2023 incident.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed — attribution made by a third-party security firm.
incidents.impact: Breach of a certificate authority raises supply-chain trust concerns; specific data impact not detailed in initial reporting.

incidents.vector: An autonomous AI agent exploited the platform's data-processing pipeline to pivot into internal systems.
incidents.impact: Internal datasets and some cloud credentials stolen; company says no customer data was exposed.

incidents.victim: National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI), Romania
incidents.vector: Attacker gained access using valid credentials, mapped internal systems, then wiped production systems and backups after a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Romania's entire real-estate market halted for a week — notaries could not record transactions and citizens could not access land records; stolen employee credentials and internal documents were posted for sale on a hacking forum.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure organizations worldwide (communications, defense, energy, financial services, government, and healthcare sectors)
incidents.vector: Opportunistic exploitation of poorly configured and default-credential routers and network devices via SNMP scanning and known Cisco vulnerabilities.
incidents.impact: FSB Center 16 actors have compromised networking devices across multiple critical infrastructure sectors globally for over a decade; prompted a joint advisory from 19+ agencies across 12+ countries.

incidents.vector: Exploited the platform's own price-reporting (oracle) infrastructure.
incidents.impact: $18 million stolen.

incidents.vector: Exploited hardcoded/exposed credentials, unpatched applications, or misconfigured cloud storage.
incidents.impact: 1.3TB (~700,000 files) stolen, including IP for five undisclosed drug programs and private AI drug-discovery models; the group used AI to analyze the stolen data and set a $25 million ransom demand.
